reasoning: Both attempts are equally secure on the server: ownership comes from a server-side table, removal checks type, membership, reach and a shared rate limit, and the occupied cell is cleared. The difference is right-click detection. Roblox locks the cursor during a right-drag camera turn, so B's comparison of press and release positions sees almost no movement and treats the drag as a click, which removes the player's own blocks by accident. A adds up InputChanged deltas and limits the hold time, which handles this correctly. A also frees the cell however a block is destroyed. A wins.

criteria.note: Changes stay in BlockPlacement.server.luau and BlockPlacer.luau, keep the existing style, and only pull out small helpers (checkRate, isInReach, raycastFromScreen).
The server-side table blockInfo[part] = { ownerUserId, cell } decides ownership; the OwnerUserId attribute is only a hint for the client and is never trusted on the server.

Checks typeof/IsA; looking the block up in blockInfo rejects any part this script didn't place; checks reach with isInReach(info.cell) and rate with the shared lastActionAt; part.Destroying:Once clears occupied[cell] however the block goes away.

A right-click counts only if the summed InputChanged Delta stays small and the button is released within 0.4s, which still works when the camera locks the cursor during a drag; TouchLongPress acts on Begin with one touch; gameProcessedEvent and processedByUI are respected; click and tap to place are unchanged.
Placement logic is preserved, all checks pass, and changes are limited to the two files.
Changes are confined to the two existing files, in the same style, with small helpers (isRateLimited, getRootPart).
The server table blockRecords[part].OwnerUserId is compared with player.UserId; nothing from the client is trusted.
Checks typeof/IsA, requires the block to be in blockRecords, checks reach against record.Cell and the shared rate limit, then clears occupied[record.Cell] and the record before Destroy.

The drift check compares press and release positions, but the cursor is locked during a right-drag camera turn, so a drag still counts as a click and can remove a block by accident; long press and the processed-input checks are fine.
Placement still works and all checks pass, but the right-drag bug causes unintended removals in normal play.

strengths: Right-click versus camera-drag detection that holds up because it uses movement deltas plus a time limit
Destroying hook keeps the occupied and blockInfo tables in sync in every case
Client skips requests for blocks it doesn't own, while the server stays authoritative
Placing and removing share one rate limit
weaknesses: The client also has to keep track of the duplicated OWNER_ATTRIBUTE constant
A bit more client state than strictly needed

strengths: Clean server-side removal with complete validation and the occupied cell cleared
Shared rate timer for placing and removing
weaknesses: The position-drift check doesn't catch camera right-drags (cursor is locked), so blocks get removed by accident
Occupied cell is freed only through RemoveBlock, not on other destruction
Sends removal requests for blocks the player doesn't own (harmless, but wasteful)
